algorithm.title: Invasive cervical cancer evaluation and staging

nodes.text: Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common cervical malignancy and often forms an exophytic mass.
Biopsy the visible lesion directly; then stage with examination and imaging.

**Other operable early-stage disease:** stage- and fertility-tailored surgery with nodal assessment.
**Locally advanced disease:** cisplatin-based chemoradiation plus brachytherapy.
Pathology and stage determine treatment; do not prescribe radical hysterectomy for every microinvasive lesion.

abnormal-uterine-bleeding.name: Abnormal uterine bleeding
abnormal-uterine-bleeding.scope: Adenomyosis, leiomyomas, endometrial polyps, ovulatory dysfunction, PALM-COEIN classification, endometrial biopsy
abnormal-uterine-bleeding.core: Abnormal uterine bleeding requires pregnancy exclusion, hemodynamic assessment and evaluation for structural disease or unopposed endometrial estrogen.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Perimenopause, PCOS, obesity, anticoagulants; lifelong heavy bleeding suggests inherited coagulopathy
Adenomyosis often multiparous; fibroids common during reproductive years

rows.label: Clues
items: Bleeding affecting quality of life, prolonged/heavy menses, intermenstrual or irregular bleeding
Tachycardia, orthostasis or syncope → clinically important blood loss
Postmenopausal bleeding requires malignancy evaluation even with a single episode

rows.label: Pathophys
items: PALM: Polyp, Adenomyosis, Leiomyoma, Malignancy/hyperplasia → structural causes
COEIN: Coagulopathy, Ovulatory dysfunction, Endometrial, Iatrogenic, Not otherwise classified
Anovulation → absent cyclic progesterone, unopposed proliferation and unstable shedding
Combined OCPs → uniform estrogen/progestin exposure **synchronizes endometrium**, preventing irregular shedding

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pregnancy test and CBC** first; pelvic examination localizes uterine versus cervical/vaginal bleeding
**Transvaginal ultrasound** evaluates structural lesions; saline sonohysterography/hysteroscopy for intracavitary disease
★ **Endometrial biopsy ≥45 years**; younger with persistent bleeding, unopposed estrogen or failed treatment
Postmenopausal bleeding: endometrial thickness >4 mm → sampling; persistent bleeding → biopsy regardless of thickness
TSH for suspected endocrine disease; coagulation/vWF testing for suggestive bleeding history

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable → IV access, blood resuscitation, urgent gynecology; tamponade or operative control if needed
Stable → high-dose combined OCP, progestin, tranexamic acid; no estrogen if prior VTE, hypertension, smoker >35
★ Long-term → **levonorgestrel IUD**, OCP/progestin; family complete, normal cavity → **ablation**; copper worsens
Fibroids: asymptomatic → **observation, any size**; symptomatic → myomectomy/embolization; hysterectomy if childbearing done
Polyp → hysteroscopic removal; adenomyosis refractory to hormones → hysterectomy

rows.label: Complications
items: Iron deficiency anemia; chronic anovulation → endometrial hyperplasia/cancer; structural lesions can impair fertility

rows.label: Prevention
items: Regular progestin exposure for chronic anovulation; replace iron and address metabolic drivers

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pregnancy complication: positive hCG; exclude ectopic pregnancy
Cervicitis: friable cervix and postcoital bleeding

table.title: Cause clues
rows: Firm irregular enlarged uterus; pressure symptoms
Labor-like pain, dilated os, beefy prolapsing tissue
Tender uterus; biopsy **plasma cells**, not neutrophils

amenorrhea.name: Amenorrhea
amenorrhea.scope: Primary amenorrhea (Turner syndrome, Mullerian agenesis, AIS), secondary amenorrhea (pregnancy, functional hypothalamic, hyperprolactinemia, thyroid, premature ovarian insufficiency, Asherman), diagnostic algorithm
amenorrhea.core: Absent menses requires pregnancy exclusion, then assessment of anatomy, estrogen status, thyroid function, prolactin, and the hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian axis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Weight loss, intense exercise, psychosocial stress; pituitary disease, dopamine-blocking drugs, thyroid dysfunction
Uterine instrumentation, chemotherapy, autoimmune disease; congenital reproductive tract or chromosomal abnormalities

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary: no menarche by 15; absent breast development by 13 also warrants evaluation
Secondary: ≥3 months absent previously regular cycles, or ≥6 months previously irregular
Galactorrhea/headache, visual symptoms, hot flashes, hirsutism, cyclic pelvic pain guide localization
Galactorrhea, hypothyroid signs → TSH first (TRH raises prolactin); unexplained prolactin → pituitary MRI

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Amenorrhea results from axis suppression, ovarian failure, chronic anovulation, or absent/obstructed outflow
Functional: energy deficit disrupts pulsatile GnRH → irregular, low gonadotropins, low estrogen

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **hCG first**, even if unlikely or premenarchal (ovulation precedes menarche); ultrasound assesses uterus, ovaries
★ TSH, prolactin, **FSH/estradiol**; low estradiol: high FSH → ovarian failure; low/normal FSH → hypothalamic/pituitary
**Progestin challenge**: bleed → anovulation (estrogen, outflow intact); no bleed → low estrogen/outflow defect, check FSH
POI before 40: ≥4 months irregular/absent cycles with FSH >25 IU/L; repeat if uncertain
Post-instrumentation amenorrhea with otherwise normal endocrine testing → saline sonography/hysteroscopy for adhesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Functional hypothalamic → **restore energy intake**, reduce excessive exercise, address eating disorder/stress
Prolactinoma → cabergoline; thyroid disease → correct thyroid function; Asherman → hysteroscopic adhesiolysis
★ POI → **estrogen replacement plus progestogen if uterus present**, usually until natural menopause age
Chronic anovulation → endometrial protection with cyclic progestogen or combined contraception; treat underlying cause
Hematocolpos → **transvaginal incision, drainage**; imperforate hymen → **cruciate hymenotomy**; ultrasound if anatomy unclear

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → infertility, low bone density; prolonged unopposed estrogen → endometrial hyperplasia
Absent uterus differs from absent ovaries: fertility options depend on anatomy and gonadal function

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, avoid overtraining/uterine injury; intermittent ovulation still requires contraception

rows.label: Mimics
items: Imperforate hymen: cyclic pain, bulging bluish hymen, hematocolpos
PCOS: hyperandrogenism with chronic anovulation, estrogen generally preserved

table.title: Primary amenorrhea: high FSH or absent uterus → karyotype

amniotic-fluid-disorders.name: Amniotic fluid disorders
amniotic-fluid-disorders.scope: Oligohydramnios (AFI <= 5 cm or single deepest pocket < 2 cm, renal anomalies, uteroplacental insufficiency), polyhydramnios (AFI >= 24 cm, maternal diabetes, GI atresia, twin-twin transfusion syndrome, anencephaly)
amniotic-fluid-disorders.core: Amniotic fluid reflects fetal urine production and swallowing; abnormal volume directs evaluation toward membrane rupture, placental disease, or fetal anomalies.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Low fluid: PPROM, post-term pregnancy, maternal vascular disease, ACE inhibitors, NSAIDs
High fluid: maternal diabetes, esophageal/duodenal atresia, anencephaly, fetal anemia; many mild cases idiopathic
Monochorionic twins: donor oligohydramnios and recipient polyhydramnios suggest twin-twin transfusion

rows.label: Clues
items: Fundal height smaller/larger than dates; fluid extremes may alter fetal movement perception
Severe excess → maternal dyspnea, distended tense abdomen; low volume → recurrent variable decelerations

rows.label: Pathophys
items: After midgestation, urine supplies most fluid; swallowing removes it
Placental hypoperfusion or absent kidneys reduces input; impaired swallowing or osmotic diuresis increases volume

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Ultrasound fluid measurement** plus anatomy survey; single deepest pocket reduces oligohydramnios overdiagnosis
Low volume → sterile speculum examination for rupture, assess kidneys/bladder, growth and umbilical Doppler
High volume → diabetes testing, detailed fetal anatomy; evaluate anemia/infection when suggested

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Isolated persistent oligohydramnios → surveillance and delivery at **36–37+6 weeks**, or diagnosis thereafter
Low fluid from PPROM/FGR → manage underlying cause; intrapartum recurrent variables may benefit from amnioinfusion
★ Polyhydramnios with severe dyspnea/discomfort → **amnioreduction**; indomethacin not solely for fluid reduction
Severe polyhydramnios, mild symptoms → **serial antenatal fetal testing**; no routine amnioreduction
Mild idiopathic polyhydramnios → spontaneous term labor; elective induction no earlier than 39 weeks

rows.label: Complications
items: Early prolonged severe low fluid → pulmonary hypoplasia, limb contractures; later → cord compression
Excess fluid → preterm labor, malpresentation, prolapsed cord, abruption after decompression, postpartum atony

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Optimize glucose control; avoid **ACE inhibitors** and nonessential NSAIDs during pregnancy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Macrosomia: large fundal height but normal fluid measurement
Incorrect dating: size discrepancy without true volume abnormality

amniotic-fluid-disorders.evidence: Polyhydramnios checked 2026-10-30: [SMFM Consult 46](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30048635/); oligohydramnios timing follows established ACOG guidance.

amniotic-fluid-embolism.name: Amniotic fluid embolism
amniotic-fluid-embolism.scope: Cardiogenic shock, respiratory failure, acute hypoxemia, disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), massive transfusion protocol, supportive critical care
amniotic-fluid-embolism.core: Abrupt hypoxemia, cardiovascular collapse, and DIC during labor or shortly after delivery suggest amniotic fluid embolism.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Labor, cesarean/vaginal delivery, placental disruption; unpredictable and usually unpreventable
Reported associations: advanced maternal age, abnormal placentation, induction; associations do not establish causation

rows.label: Clues
items: Sudden dyspnea, cyanosis, agitation, seizure, profound hypotension, fetal bradycardia
★ **Bleeding from IV sites or uterine hemorrhage** with falling fibrinogen suggests consumptive coagulopathy
May present chiefly as coagulopathy; absence of the full triad early does not exclude disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Maternal inflammatory response to amniotic components triggers pulmonary vasoconstriction and coagulation activation
Acute right ventricular failure may progress to left ventricular dysfunction and pulmonary edema

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis of exclusion**; no definitive blood test or imaging marker
ABG, CBC, PT/aPTT, fibrinogen, crossmatch; bedside echocardiography helps characterize shock
Fetal squamous cells in pulmonary circulation are neither necessary nor specific
Exclude hemorrhage, pulmonary thromboembolism, anaphylaxis, high neuraxial block, eclampsia without delaying resuscitation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **High-quality CPR**, left uterine displacement, oxygenation/intubation; activate obstetric/anesthesia/critical-care teams
Vasopressors/inotropes guided by echocardiography; avoid fluid overload with RV failure
★ **Massive transfusion protocol**: red cells, plasma, platelets; replace fibrinogen with cryoprecipitate/concentrate
Arrest, uterus ≥umbilicus, no ROSC → resuscitative delivery: start by 4 minutes, birth by 5
Operate at arrest location without transport delay; consider ECMO for refractory cardiopulmonary failure

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoxic brain injury, multiorgan failure, exsanguination, maternal death; fetal hypoxic injury/death

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pulmonary embolism: thrombotic risk, RV strain; immediate profound DIC less characteristic
Anaphylaxis: trigger exposure, urticaria/bronchospasm; treat epinephrine
Hemorrhagic shock: bleeding precedes collapse, rather than unexplained respiratory failure first

amniotic-fluid-embolism.evidence: Resuscitation checked 2026-10-30: [SMFM updated AFE checklist, 2026](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13565333/); clinical patterns established teaching.

antepartum-bleeding.name: Antepartum bleeding
antepartum-bleeding.scope: Placenta previa, placental abruption, vasa previa, uterine rupture, transabdominal ultrasound before digital exam, Kleihauer-Betke test, emergent cesarean delivery
antepartum-bleeding.core: Bleeding in later pregnancy requires immediate maternal stabilization and fetal assessment, followed by placental localization before any digital cervical examination.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Previa: prior cesarean, multiparity; abruption: hypertension, cocaine, trauma, prior abruption
Vasa previa: velamentous cord, accessory placental lobe, IVF; rupture: uterine scar, obstructed labor

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Shock may exceed visible blood loss** with concealed abruption or internal hemorrhage
Assess uterine tone, pain, contractions, fetal tracing, membrane status; bleeding volume alone is unreliable

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Maternal placental bleeding versus fetal vessel hemorrhage; vasa previa can rapidly exsanguinate fetus
Placental separation or uterine disruption compromises oxygen delivery independent of maternal external blood loss

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ CBC, type/crossmatch, coagulation studies including fibrinogen; continuous fetal monitoring if viable
★ **Ultrasound before digital examination**; transabdominal first; transvaginal safely clarifies placenta–cervix relationship
Normal ultrasound does not exclude abruption; suspected rupture is a clinical emergency
Rh-negative bleeding/trauma → Kleihauer–Betke or flow cytometry quantifies fetomaternal hemorrhage for anti-D dosing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ ABCs, two large IVs, blood products when needed; **do not delay delivery for imaging if unstable**
Hemorrhage/fetal compromise → emergency cesarean; rupture → laparotomy, uterine repair or hysterectomy
Stable preterm previa → observation, pelvic rest, corticosteroids when eligible; planned cesarean before labor
Abruption: deliver if significant or compromised; vaginal birth possible when stable and imminent or fetal demise
Unsensitized Rh-negative patient → anti-D immunoglobulin; correct abruption-associated coagulopathy

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemorrhagic shock, DIC, AKI, hysterectomy; fetal hypoxia, death, prematurity
Previa plus cesarean scar increases placenta accreta spectrum risk and operative hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Control BP, avoid cocaine/tobacco; prenatal placental/cord localization and planned high-risk delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bloody show: small mucus-streaked bleeding with cervical change
Cervical lesion: contact bleeding, visible source on speculum examination

table.title: Critical distinctions
rows: Bleeding after rupture; sudden fetal bradycardia
Scarred uterus; sudden pain, lost station, fetal bradycardia

appendicitis.name: Appendicitis
appendicitis.scope: Acute appendicitis, clinical presentation, pediatric and pregnancy considerations, imaging (ultrasound, CT), surgical management
appendicitis.core: Periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, followed by anorexia and nausea, suggests appendiceal inflammation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Adolescents/young adults; luminal obstruction by lymphoid hyperplasia or fecalith
Older adults may have obstructing neoplasm; immunosuppression can blunt findings

rows.label: Clues
items: McBurney tenderness, guarding, fever; Rovsing, psoas, or obturator signs depend on position
★ **Diffuse peritonitis, toxicity, hypotension** → perforation/sepsis until proven otherwise
Young children: nonspecific symptoms and rapid progression; pregnancy: displaced appendix, less reliable examination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Luminal obstruction → distention, venous congestion, bacterial invasion → ischemia/perforation
Visceral midgut pain precedes focal parietal peritoneal irritation

rows.label: Dx
items: CBC, urinalysis, **pregnancy test** in reproductive-age patients; pyuria does not exclude appendicitis
★ Stable nonpregnant adult → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast** when diagnosis uncertain
★ Child/pregnancy → **ultrasound first**; nondiagnostic → MRI without gadolinium, or CT in nonpregnant child
Noncompressible enlarged appendix >6 mm with periappendiceal inflammation supports diagnosis
Clear peritonitis → surgical evaluation; do not delay necessary operation for repeated imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ NPO, **IV fluids, IV opioids, ceftriaxone + metronidazole**, surgical consultation; opioids do not obscure exam
Laparoscopic appendectomy definitive; do not withhold necessary surgery during pregnancy
Selected uncomplicated cases → antibiotics after shared decision; recurrence/failure higher, especially with appendicolith
Localized abscess/phlegmon in stable patient → antibiotics ± image-guided drainage; follow-up based on age/risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Perforation, abscess, peritonitis, sepsis, ileus
Postoperative wound infection, intra-abdominal collection, adhesional obstruction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, adnexal findings
Ovarian torsion: sudden unilateral pelvic pain; gastroenteritis: diarrhea prominent before diffuse cramping
Mesenteric adenitis: viral prodrome, normal appendix on imaging

appendicitis.evidence: Not checked online; established general-surgery evaluation and treatment principles.

bartholin-gland-cyst-and-abscess.name: Bartholin gland cyst and abscess
bartholin-gland-cyst-and-abscess.scope: Asymptomatic cyst, symptomatic cyst, acute Bartholin abscess, incision and drainage, Word catheter placement, marsupialization, excision for recurrent or older women
bartholin-gland-cyst-and-abscess.core: Obstructed posterior vestibular gland causing a cyst or abscess; durable drainage prevents recurrence, and age determines the need for malignancy assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive age, prior duct obstruction, previous cyst/abscess; usually polymicrobial vaginal/enteric flora
STIs may coexist but most abscesses are not solely gonococcal or chlamydial

rows.label: Clues
items: Cyst: soft fluctuant, often painless; abscess: marked tenderness, erythema, difficulty sitting/walking
Gland location near 4 or 8 o'clock at vaginal opening; usually unilateral
Firm, fixed, irregular, recurrent, or postmenopausal lesion → malignancy concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Duct occlusion retains gland secretions; bacterial infection produces purulence
Drainage without an epithelialized outlet allows rapid closure and recurrence

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical vulvar examination**; assess cellulitis, systemic illness, pregnancy, immune status
GC/chlamydia NAAT when sexual risk or cervicitis; culture selected recurrent/severe infections
★ **Biopsy at age ≥40 or suspicious mass**; imaging unnecessary for typical superficial lesion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Management branches below; **Word catheter about 4 weeks** permits an epithelialized drainage tract
★ Avoid **incision alone or needle aspiration**: rapid closure causes recurrence
Antibiotics only for cellulitis, systemic infection, immunocompromise, or confirmed STI; uncomplicated drainage needs none
Persistent recurrence → gland excision after acute inflammation settles

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent abscess, surrounding cellulitis, rare sepsis; early catheter expulsion can compromise tract formation
Excision → bleeding, scarring, dyspareunia; older patients risk missed gland malignancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Complete catheter follow-up, hygiene without irritating products; condoms/STI treatment for exposure-related infection
No proven universal prevention of duct obstruction; return promptly for recurrent pain, fever, or mass

rows.label: Mimics
items: Skene duct cyst: periurethral/anterior location
Epidermal inclusion cyst: superficial skin nodule, possible punctum
Hidradenitis: recurrent multiple intertriginous nodules, sinus tracts

bartholin-gland-cyst-and-abscess.evidence: Not checked online; established gynecologic office-procedure teaching.

benign-breast-conditions.name: Benign breast conditions
benign-breast-conditions.scope: Fibroadenoma, fibrocystic changes, intraductal papilloma, breast cyst, fat necrosis, galactocele, breast abscess
benign-breast-conditions.core: Breast symptoms require age-directed imaging and clinical–radiologic concordance; a benign-appearing examination alone cannot exclude malignancy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive hormonal cycling; milk stasis; breast trauma or prior surgery
Smoking predisposes to recurrent subareolar abscess
**Cracked, excoriated nipples** → main portal of entry for lactational mastitis

rows.label: Clues
items: Galactocele: cystic lactational/postlactational mass, no inflammation, varies with feeds; fat–fluid level on imaging
Mastitis: focal tender erythema, fever, no fluctuance; abscess adds **fluctuance**; often Staphylococcus aureus
★ Spontaneous unilateral **bloody single-duct discharge** → usually **papilloma**; exclude malignancy, persistent → surgical evaluation
Nonbloody discharge only on expression, normal exam → **physiologic**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hormone-responsive stromal/glandular tissue produces cyclic changes; duct obstruction causes retained secretions
Adipose injury causes inflammatory necrosis and calcification that can resemble cancer

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Palpable mass **<30 years → ultrasound**; ≥30 → diagnostic mammography with targeted ultrasound
Suspicious solid lesion or imaging–exam discordance → **core needle biopsy**
Simple cyst: anechoic, thin-walled, posterior enhancement; no solid component
Nonlactational abscess or persistent inflammation after antibiotics → exclude underlying carcinoma
Cyclic bilateral nodularity, no dominant mass → **reexamine after menses**, before imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Painful simple cyst → aspiration; nonbloody fluid + full collapse → benign; bloody fluid/residual mass → **biopsy**
Fibroadenoma → observe when concordant; excise if rapidly enlarging, large or symptomatic
Breast pain, no mass, young, normal exam → **reassurance**; fibrocystic pain → supportive bra, topical/oral NSAID
★ Mastitis → **dicloxacillin/cephalexin**, keep breastfeeding/pumping; abscess → add needle/incision drainage; MRSA → clindamycin
Tender lactating lump, no erythema/fever → **warm compresses**, keep nursing; persistent galactocele → aspiration

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent periductal abscess → fistula; incomplete drainage → persistent infection
Proliferative lesions with atypia increase future cancer risk; simple cysts do not

rows.label: Prevention
items: Effective breast emptying during lactation; smoking cessation for recurrent periductal disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cancer: irregular fixed mass, retraction or suspicious nodes
Phyllodes: rapidly enlarging fibroepithelial mass requiring excision

table.title: Common benign findings
rows: Early postpartum; bilateral tense tender breasts, low fever

cervical-cancer-screening.name: Cervical Cancer Screening
cervical-cancer-screening.scope: USPSTF guidelines by age (Pap smear alone 21-29, Pap with hrHPV cotesting or hrHPV alone 30-65), screening cessation, post-hysterectomy
cervical-cancer-screening.core: Screen average-risk people with a cervix from age 21; age, prior results, and cervical precancer history determine testing and cessation.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **Average-risk cervix present**; sexual history and HPV vaccination do not alter schedule
HIV, immunosuppression, DES exposure, prior CIN 2+ → separate surveillance pathways
HIV: **cytology annually**; every 3 years only after 3 consecutive normal results

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Stop after 65 only with **adequate negative prior screening** and no high-risk history
Adequate: 3 negative cytology/2 HPV-based tests over 10 years; latest within 5
Total benign hysterectomy, no CIN 2+/cancer → stop; supracervical hysterectomy → continue

rows.label: Test
items: Choose one age-specific strategy below; annual testing increases unnecessary procedures

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ **HPV 16/18 or high-grade cytology → colposcopy**, including pregnancy, <25; others: risk assessment
CIN 2+ even hysterectomy → vaginal-cuff HPV-based testing ≥25 years; older exams: annual Pap

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Postcoital bleeding or visible lesion → diagnostic evaluation**, regardless of screening interval
Under 21: no routine screening; unknown/inadequate history after 65 → continue
USPSTF 2018 final schedule below; later draft self-collection proposals do not replace final guidance

table.title: USPSTF age-based choices
rows: Primary hrHPV or cotest every 5 years

cervical-neoplasia.name: Cervical neoplasia
cervical-neoplasia.scope: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, invasive cervical cancer, squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, colposcopy
cervical-neoplasia.core: Persistent high-risk HPV drives cervical precancer and cancer; abnormal screening needs risk-based evaluation, while visible symptomatic lesions require biopsy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HPV 16/18 persistence, smoking, HIV/immunosuppression, limited screening access

rows.label: Clues
items: CIN usually asymptomatic; invasive disease → postcoital/intermenstrual bleeding, watery discharge
Friable cervical mass, pelvic pain; hydronephrosis or leg edema suggests advanced spread

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Viral E6 degrades p53; E7 inactivates Rb → transformation-zone dysplasia
Squamous carcinoma most common; adenocarcinoma arises in endocervical glands

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Visible lesion → biopsy**, regardless of prior normal Pap/HPV result
★ HPV 16/18 positivity, ASC-H or AGC → **colposcopy**, even with otherwise reassuring screening
AGC → endocervical sampling; add endometrial biopsy at ≥35 or with endometrial risk factors
Colposcopy-directed biopsy diagnoses CIN; invasive cancer → pelvic examination, MRI/PET-CT for extent
Pregnancy → risk-based colposcopy; no endocervical curettage or expedited excision

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ CIN 3 → **cone/LEEP** outside pregnancy; unseen SCJ → no ablation; fertility concerns → observe CIN 2
CIN 1 → observation; select nonpregnant patients ≥25 with very high risk → expedited excision
AIS → diagnostic excision; hysterectomy after childbearing if margins adequately assessed
Microinvasive → conization if preserving fertility, else **simple hysterectomy**; other early invasive → radical hysterectomy
Locally advanced → cisplatin-based chemoradiation plus brachytherapy

rows.label: Complications
items: Ureteral obstruction, fistulas, metastases; cervical excision increases subsequent preterm-birth risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **HPV vaccination** plus age-based screening; vaccination does not eliminate screening
After treated CIN 2/3/AIS: initial intensive HPV surveillance, then every 3 years for ≥25 years

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervicitis: mucopurulent discharge and positive STI testing
Endometrial cancer: uterine-source bleeding; benign ectropion: smooth eversion without destructive lesion

table.title: Histologic grade
rows: More than two-thirds; basement membrane intact

chlamydia-infection.name: Chlamydia infection
chlamydia-infection.scope: Chlamydia trachomatis, nongonococcal urethritis, cervicitis, lymphogranuloma venereum, neonatal conjunctivitis and pneumonia, NAAT screening and diagnosis, doxycycline and azithromycin
chlamydia-infection.core: Often silent sexually transmitted intracellular infection causing urethritis or cervicitis; untreated infection threatens fertility and can infect newborns during delivery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age <25 years, new/multiple partners, inconsistent condom use, infected partner; perinatal exposure

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, scant discharge, sterile pyuria; friable cervix, mucopurulent discharge, postcoital/intermenstrual bleeding
★ Neonatal conjunctivitis at **5–12 days**; afebrile staccato pneumonia at **1–3 months**
LGV: transient painless genital ulcer → tender inguinal nodes/buboes or invasive proctocolitis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: C. trachomatis: obligate intracellular bacterium; D–K serovars cause genital/perinatal infection, L1–L3 cause LGV

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **NAAT**: vaginal swab preferred in women; first-catch urine in men; rectal swab after exposure
Test for gonorrhea, HIV, syphilis; fever, pelvic pain, cervical motion tenderness → evaluate for PID
Infant conjunctival testing requires epithelial cells; nasopharyngeal testing for pneumonia
Sexually active MSM: annual site-specific screening; every 3–6 months with persistent high risk

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Uncomplicated infection → **doxycycline for 7 days**; LGV → 21 days
★ Pregnancy → **azithromycin**, single dose; alternative when adherence doubtful, less reliable for rectal infection
Neonatal disease → oral erythromycin for 14 days; azithromycin alternative; topical treatment alone inadequate
Gonorrhea suspected or detected → add ceftriaxone; PID requires broader multidrug coverage

rows.label: Complications
items: PID → tubal infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain; epididymitis, reactive arthritis
LGV → rectal strictures/fistulas; infant macrolides → hypertrophic pyloric stenosis risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Treat partners from preceding **60 days**; expedited partner treatment where legal
Abstain until 7-day course completed or 7 days after single dose, and partners treated
★ **Annual NAAT**: sexually active women <25 despite condoms; older if risk; pregnancy entry; Pap from 21
Retest at 3 months; pregnancy test-of-cure at 4 weeks; neonatal eye ointment does not prevent chlamydia

rows.label: Mimics
items: Gonorrhea: copious purulent discharge, Gram-stain intracellular diplococci; **neutrophils alone** → nongonococcal urethritis, usually chlamydia
M. genitalium: persistent nongonococcal urethritis after doxycycline; separate NAAT
HSV: painful ulcers and external dysuria rather than isolated cervical discharge
Cystitis: suprapubic tenderness, bacteriuria; urethritis → **distal anterior vaginal wall tenderness**, sterile pyuria

congenital-infections.name: Congenital infections
congenital-infections.scope: Cytomegalovirus (sensorineural hearing loss, periventricular calcifications), Toxoplasmosis (chorioretinitis), Parvovirus B19 (hydrops), Rubella, Varicella, Zika, screening and diagnosis
congenital-infections.core: Congenital infection causes growth restriction, hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, thrombocytopenia, or hydrops; organ-specific patterns identify the pathogen.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: CMV: toddler saliva/urine; toxoplasma: undercooked meat, cat feces; B19: child with slapped-cheek rash
Absent rubella/varicella immunity; mosquito exposure or sexual transmission in Zika-risk areas

rows.label: Clues
items: Petechiae/blueberry-muffin lesions, abnormal fetal ultrasound; many infected newborns initially appear well
★ B19 hydrops: cardiomegaly, ascites, edema without red-cell alloantibodies
Maternal rash: B19 → slapped cheek, then reticular limb rash; rubella → descending rash, postauricular nodes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transplacental infection disrupts organogenesis; later exposure may cause inflammation or marrow suppression
Toxoplasma transmission increases with gestational age; earlier infection causes more severe injury

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Maternal exposure → pathogen-specific **IgG/IgM**, paired titers or avidity; isolated IgM needs confirmation
★ CMV newborn diagnosis: saliva PCR then confirm urine PCR **within 21 days**
Suspected fetal infection → targeted ultrasound, pathogen-specific amniotic-fluid PCR; B19 → serial MCA Doppler
Prenatal rubella IgG routinely; no universal US maternal CMV, toxoplasma, or B19 screening

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic congenital CMV → **valganciclovir**, monitor CBC and liver tests
Congenital toxoplasmosis → pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + leucovorin; maternal regimen depends on fetal infection
B19 severe fetal anemia → intrauterine transfusion; rubella/Zika structural injury → supportive care
Maternal varicella exposure without immunity → varicella-zoster immune globulin; maternal pneumonia → IV acyclovir
Maternal varicella onset 5 days before to 2 days after delivery → **newborn VZIG**

rows.label: Complications
items: Stillbirth, neurodevelopmental disability; delayed/progressive hearing loss requires longitudinal audiology

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Rubella/varicella vaccination before pregnancy or postpartum; **live vaccines contraindicated during pregnancy**
Handwashing after diapers; cook meat, avoid litter handling; mosquito precautions and Zika exposure counseling
Term newborn of varicella-immune mother: transplacental IgG protects → no prophylaxis after exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aneuploidy: abnormal genetic testing rather than pathogen testing
Rh disease: positive maternal antibody screen with fetal anemia

table.title: Discriminating congenital patterns
rows: Periventricular calcifications, microcephaly, sensorineural hearing loss, chorioretinitis
Severe microcephaly, subcortical calcifications, ocular abnormalities

congenital-infections.evidence: CMV testing checked 2026-10-30: [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/cytomegalovirus/hcp/clinical-overview/index.html); remaining pathogen patterns established teaching.

contraception.name: Contraception
contraception.scope: Combined oral contraceptives, progestin-only pills, implant, intrauterine devices, tubal sterilization
contraception.core: Choose contraception through shared decisions about efficacy, bleeding, reversibility, adherence, and estrogen-related vascular risk.

rows.label: Who
items: Anyone seeking pregnancy prevention; adolescents and nulliparous patients can use IUDs or implants
Healthy patient: blood pressure suffices; **no pelvic exam** needed before oral contraceptives

rows.label: Schedule
items: Pills daily; depot medroxyprogesterone every 3 months; implants/IUDs last years (product-dependent)
★ Emergency contraception ≤**5 days**: copper IUD/ulipristal; levonorgestrel ≤72 h, no medical contraindications
Progestin-only pills: daily timing crucial; norethindrone less forgiving than drospirenone

rows.label: Special groups
items: Breastfeeding (estrogen lowers milk volume, protein) or estrogen contraindication → progestin-only or copper IUD
Current breast cancer → copper IUD; avoid hormonal methods
Prior VTE, poor adherence → **IUD/implant** (depot raises VTE risk); older exams: depot, avoid IUD after STI

rows.label: Choice
items: Combined pills: suppress ovulation, improve acne/cramps, reduce endometrial/ovarian cancer risk
★ **LARC** minimizes adherence failures; condoms add STI protection
Tubal sterilization: permanent; counsel regret, alternatives, surgical risk, ectopic risk after failure

rows.label: Contraindications
items: ★ Estrogen: **migraine with aura, prior VTE/thrombophilia**, hypertension (stop pill), early postpartum
Smoking age ≥35: combined methods usually avoid; ≥15 cigarettes/day → absolute contraindication
IUD: pregnancy, cervicitis/PID, distorted cavity (non-distorting fibroid OK); copper: also Wilson disease

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Same-day STI screening need not delay insertion without cervicitis; prior PID alone permits IUD
Sterilization: voluntary informed consent; no required partner approval, parity, or marital status
After ulipristal, wait 5 days before progestin; backup contraception needed after hormonal restart

table.title: Long-acting choices
rows: Treats heavy menses; atrophy → expected benign amenorrhea

dysmenorrhea.name: Dysmenorrhea
dysmenorrhea.scope: Primary dysmenorrhea, secondary dysmenorrhea (endometriosis, adenomyosis, cervical stenosis), hematometra, NSAIDs, combined oral contraceptives
dysmenorrhea.core: Painful menstruation: primary disease begins after ovulatory cycles develop; later-onset, progressive, or refractory pain suggests pelvic pathology.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Early menarche, heavy/prolonged flow, family history, smoking
Prior cervical excision/ablation → stenosis; endometriosis and adenomyosis produce secondary symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Suprapubic cramping radiating to back/thighs, nausea, diarrhea, headache
★ **Dyspareunia, abnormal bleeding, infertility**, or pain outside menses → secondary cause
Amenorrhea or scant flow after cervical procedure with cyclic pain → retained menstrual blood

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Progesterone withdrawal → endometrial prostaglandins → uterine hypercontractility and ischemia
Outflow obstruction traps blood in uterine cavity → hematometra

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Classic adolescent presentation without red flags → **clinical diagnosis**, no initial imaging
Sexual activity → pregnancy test; infection risks → gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT
Secondary features → pelvic examination and **transvaginal ultrasound**; transabdominal imaging if needed
No improvement after 3–6 months despite adherence → investigate secondary disease, consider laparoscopy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **NSAIDs**, starting 1–2 days before expected bleeding through first 2–3 days
★ Inadequate response/contraception desired → **combined OCP** or progestin; continuous suppression may help
Heat, exercise; avoid NSAIDs with active ulcer disease or significant renal dysfunction
Treat underlying lesion; cervical stenosis with hematometra → cervical dilation/drainage

rows.label: Complications
items: School/work absence, sleep disturbance; untreated secondary disease may impair fertility
Analgesic adverse effects: GI bleeding, renal injury; estrogen-containing contraception → VTE risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Track cycles and preempt pain; ongoing menstrual suppression reduces recurrence when pregnancy not desired

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, nonmenstrual bleeding, possible instability
PID: fever, mucopurulent discharge, cervical motion tenderness

table.title: Secondary patterns
rows: Posterior nodularity; ultrasound may be normal
Heavy bleeding, boggy uniformly enlarged uterus

dysmenorrhea.evidence: Not checked online; established adolescent gynecology and pelvic-pain teaching.

ectopic-pregnancy.name: Ectopic pregnancy
ectopic-pregnancy.scope: Diagnosis (beta-hCG, transvaginal ultrasound, discriminatory zone), unruptured ectopic pregnancy, medical management (methotrexate), ruptured ectopic pregnancy, surgical management
ectopic-pregnancy.core: Pregnancy implanted outside the endometrial cavity, usually tubal; early pregnancy with pelvic pain or bleeding requires localization and rupture assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior ectopic, PID/tubal damage, tubal surgery, infertility treatment, smoking
IUDs prevent pregnancy overall; pregnancy despite IUD has higher ectopic proportion; many cases lack risks

rows.label: Clues
items: Amenorrhea, unilateral pelvic pain, spotting; cervical motion/adnexal tenderness nonspecific
★ **Syncope, shoulder-tip pain, peritoneal signs, hypotension** → hemoperitoneum/rupture
Heterotopic pregnancy possible despite visualized intrauterine pregnancy, particularly after assisted reproduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired tubal transport → extrauterine trophoblastic implantation, invasion, hemorrhage
Methotrexate inhibits folate-dependent DNA synthesis in proliferating trophoblast

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pregnancy test → quantitative beta-hCG + transvaginal ultrasound**; ultrasound regardless of hCG when symptomatic
Extrauterine yolk sac/embryo diagnostic; adnexal mass/free fluid supportive; empty uterus alone insufficient
★ Stable pregnancy of unknown location → **repeat hCG in 48 hours**, serial ultrasound until resolved/localized
Subnormal 48-hour hCG rise + empty uterus + pain → suspect **ectopic**; rapid fall favors miscarriage
Discriminatory threshold up to 3,500 mIU/mL protects viable IUP; abnormal rise/fall cannot establish location

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable/rupture concern → **IV access, blood resuscitation, urgent laparotomy**; do not await serial hCG
Confirmed unruptured, stable, reliable follow-up, hCG <5,000, mass <3.5 cm, no fetal heartbeat → consider **methotrexate**
Avoid methotrexate: viable IUP, breastfeeding, hepatic/renal disease, cytopenias, immunodeficiency, unreliable follow-up
Postmethotrexate hCG days 4/7: fall ≥15% → weekly until negative; inadequate fall → reassess/re-dose/surgery

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemorrhagic shock, death, tubal loss, recurrence, impaired fertility
Methotrexate: mucositis, hepatotoxicity, marrow suppression; rupture remains possible despite falling hCG

rows.label: Prevention
items: Treat/prevent STIs, smoking cessation; prior ectopic → early ultrasound in subsequent pregnancy
Methotrexate counseling: avoid alcohol, folate supplements, intercourse until resolution; avoid conception for 3 months
Unsensitized Rh-negative ectopic → Rh(D) immune globulin; provide return precautions for escalating pain/dizziness

rows.label: Mimics
items: Miscarriage: intrauterine pregnancy loss; passage of decidual tissue alone does not prove IUP
Hemorrhagic corpus luteum: ovarian source, may coexist with normal pregnancy
Ovarian torsion: abrupt severe unilateral pain, enlarged ovary

table.title: Alternative definitive branches
rows: Stable, minimal symptoms, low declining hCG
Selected expectant management with reliable surveillance
Heartbeat, high hCG, severe pain, or contraindication

ectopic-pregnancy.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG ectopic pregnancy](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/ectopic-pregnancy), [NICE tubal ectopic management](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/NG126/chapter/management-of-tubal-ectopic-pregnancy); conservative discriminatory threshold established ACOG teaching.

fetal-growth-restriction.name: Fetal growth restriction
fetal-growth-restriction.scope: Symmetric vs asymmetric FGR, uteroplacental insufficiency, chromosomal anomalies, congenital infections, umbilical artery Doppler surveillance, oligohydramnios
fetal-growth-restriction.core: Estimated fetal weight or abdominal circumference below the 10th percentile requires evaluation for placental dysfunction and fetal disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Maternal hypertension, preeclampsia, renal/vascular disease, smoking, cocaine, malnutrition, prior affected pregnancy
Aneuploidy, structural anomalies, CMV; multiple gestation

rows.label: Clues
items: Fundal height lag >3 cm, decreased movement, oligohydramnios; sometimes abnormal maternal placental disease markers
★ **EFW <3rd percentile** indicates severe disease; normal-size parents do not establish constitutional smallness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental resistance reduces oxygen/nutrients; redistribution preserves cerebral over abdominal growth
Low fetal renal perfusion reduces urine production and fluid volume

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Ultrasound biometry using reliable dating → detailed anatomy; serial growth generally every 3–4 weeks
★ **Umbilical artery Doppler every 1–2 weeks**; absent (AEDV)/reversed (REDV) diastolic velocity → intensified surveillance
Weekly NST after viability; increase frequency with Doppler deterioration or maternal comorbidity
Early <32 weeks, unexplained or anomalous → offer amniocentesis/microarray; CMV PCR if amniocentesis chosen
Do not order indiscriminate TORCH panels without exposure or suggestive findings

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Reversed flow → **hospitalization**, corticosteroids, frequent cardiotocography, delivery planning
Anticipated preterm birth → betamethasone; magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection before 32 weeks
Nonreassuring testing/maternal deterioration → earlier delivery; absent/reversed flow may favor cesarean
Bed rest, sildenafil, and LMWH solely to treat/prevent FGR provide no established benefit

rows.label: Complications
items: Stillbirth, intrapartum intolerance, neonatal hypoglycemia, hypothermia, polycythemia; later metabolic/cardiovascular risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Tobacco/drug cessation, maternal disease control; low-dose aspirin when preeclampsia-risk criteria met

rows.label: Mimics
items: Incorrect dates: early ultrasound establishes gestational age
Constitutionally small fetus: reassuring interval growth and normal Doppler without placental disease

table.title: Patterns and delivery in otherwise stable disease
rows: Often later placental insufficiency; patterns overlap

gestational-diabetes-mellitus.name: Gestational diabetes mellitus
gestational-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Screening (50g oral glucose challenge at 24-28 weeks), diagnostic 3-hour 100g test, glycemic targets, nutritional therapy, insulin, fetal and neonatal complications (macrosomia, hypoglycemia, RDS, polycythemia)
gestational-diabetes-mellitus.core: Pregnancy-induced insulin resistance unmasks hyperglycemia, increasing fetal insulin secretion and growth; screen routinely at 24–28 weeks.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, prior GDM/macrosomia, family history of type 2 diabetes, PCOS
High-risk patients need early assessment for previously unrecognized overt diabetes

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; excessive fetal growth or polyhydramnios may prompt evaluation
Early marked hyperglycemia suggests preexisting diabetes rather than typical later-onset GDM

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental hormones increase maternal insulin requirements; inadequate beta-cell compensation causes dysglycemia
Maternal glucose crosses placenta; insulin does not; fetal hyperinsulinemia persists briefly after birth
Fetal hyperinsulinemia → macrosomia; antagonizes cortisol → less surfactant, **RDS**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Two-step screen: **nonfasting 50 g challenge**, 1-hour threshold 130–140 mg/dL by local protocol
Positive challenge → fasting 100 g, 3-hour OGTT; **≥2 abnormal values** diagnose GDM
Alternative one-step 75 g OGTT: fasting ≥92, 1-hour ≥180, or 2-hour ≥153 mg/dL
HbA1c alone does not replace pregnancy glucose testing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First: **individualized nutrition, activity, home glucose monitoring**; avoid severe carbohydrate restriction
★ Targets: fasting **<95**, 1-hour <140, or 2-hour <120 mg/dL
Above targets despite lifestyle → **insulin preferred**; metformin crosses placenta, counsel if used
Medication need or poor control → fetal surveillance; delivery timing depends on control and obstetric findings
Suspected fetal weight ≥4,500 g with diabetes → discuss planned cesarean

rows.label: Complications
items: Maternal: preeclampsia, cesarean delivery, future type 2 diabetes
Fetal: macrosomia, shoulder dystocia, birth trauma; poor control increases stillbirth risk
Neonate: **hypoglycemia**, RDS, polycythemia, jaundice; congenital anomalies mainly reflect pregestational diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Postpartum **75 g OGTT at 4–12 weeks**; lifelong diabetes testing every 1–3 years
Breastfeeding, weight management, activity; most GDM insulin needs resolve after placental delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pregestational diabetes: overt diagnostic-range hyperglycemia early in pregnancy
Physiologic glycosuria: lower renal threshold without diagnostic blood glucose abnormalities

gestational-trophoblastic-disease.name: Gestational trophoblastic disease
gestational-trophoblastic-disease.scope: Complete hydatidiform mole, partial hydatidiform mole, choriocarcinoma, suction curettage, serial beta-hCG surveillance, contraception
gestational-trophoblastic-disease.core: Abnormal trophoblastic proliferation causes excessive hCG, bleeding, and vesicular placental tissue; persistent hCG after evacuation suggests gestational trophoblastic neoplasia.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior molar pregnancy, extremes of reproductive age; choriocarcinoma can follow any pregnancy

rows.label: Clues
items: Vaginal bleeding, hyperemesis, uterus larger than dates, bilateral theca lutein cysts
★ **Preeclampsia before 20 weeks** or gestational thyrotoxicosis → suspect mole
Postpregnancy bleeding with cough/hemoptysis or neurologic symptoms → metastatic trophoblastic malignancy

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Abnormal fertilization produces proliferative hydropic villi; high hCG stimulates thyroid and ovarian receptors
Choriocarcinoma lacks chorionic villi and spreads hematogenously, especially to lungs, vagina, brain

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Quantitative **β-hCG + pelvic ultrasound**; snowstorm/multicystic placental appearance may be absent early
Evacuated tissue histopathology confirms; p57 absent in complete mole, retained in partial mole
★ Postevacuation **hCG plateau over 3 weeks or rise over 2 weeks** → evaluate GTN
Suspected neoplasia → chest imaging and stage/risk assessment; avoid biopsy of vascular vaginal metastasis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Stabilize bleeding → **suction curettage**; send tissue; give anti-D if Rh-negative
Hysterectomy an option when fertility not desired; surveillance remains necessary
Low-risk GTN → methotrexate or actinomycin D; high-risk → multiagent chemotherapy
hCG every 1–2 weeks until normal; partial: reconfirm after 1 month; complete: monthly for 6 months

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemorrhage, thyroid storm, early hypertensive disease, invasive mole, metastatic malignancy
Chemotherapy toxicity; prognosis often excellent even with metastatic disease when treated

rows.label: Prevention
items: Reliable contraception during hCG surveillance; combined OCPs acceptable; defer pregnancy until follow-up complete
Future pregnancy → early ultrasound and postpregnancy hCG assessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Multiple gestation: high hCG with recognizable normally developing fetuses
Missed abortion: nonviable gestation without trophoblastic overgrowth

table.title: Molar subtypes
rows: Usually triploid; maternal + two paternal sets

gestational-trophoblastic-disease.evidence: Surveillance checked 2026-10-30: [FIGO 2025 update](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12411817/); remaining pathology established teaching.

herpes-simplex-virus.name: Herpes simplex virus
herpes-simplex-virus.scope: HSV-1 and HSV-2, genital herpes, neonatal herpes, herpes labialis, eczema herpeticum, acyclovir
herpes-simplex-virus.core: Painful grouped vesicles recurring at mucocutaneous sites reflect latent HSV reactivation; neonatal infection and disseminated disease require urgent systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Skin/mucosal contact, asymptomatic shedding, new sexual partners; either HSV type can cause genital disease
Immunosuppression, atopic dermatitis; neonatal risk highest with newly acquired maternal infection near delivery

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary genital: fever, tender nodes, dysuria, painful ulcers, 2–3 weeks; recurrences milder, resolve within 1 week
Labialis: tingling prodrome, vermilion cluster; **whitlow**: painful grouped finger vesicles after oral-secretion exposure
★ **Monomorphic punched-out erosions in eczema** → eczema herpeticum; ocular symptoms threaten vision
Neonate: sepsislike illness, vesicles sometimes absent; seizures/hepatitis suggest CNS or disseminated disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: HSV establishes sensory ganglion latency; stress, illness, UV exposure trigger reactivation
Genital HSV-2 recurs/sheds more than genital HSV-1

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Active lesion → **HSV PCR/NAAT with typing**; culture less sensitive as lesions heal
Encephalitis/neonatal CNS concern, **lymphocytic CSF with RBCs** → CSF HSV PCR; early negative may require repeat
Neonate → lesion/surface, blood, CSF testing plus liver enzymes; treat while testing
No routine type-specific serology screening or HSV IgM

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First genital episode → **oral acyclovir or valacyclovir for 7–10 days**; start before results
Recurrence → prompt episodic dosing at prodrome; frequent/distressing episodes → daily suppressive valacyclovir
★ Neonatal, CNS, disseminated disease or severe eczema herpeticum → **IV acyclovir**
Pregnancy: acyclovir/valacyclovir from 36 weeks; labor lesions/prodrome → cesarean; neither → vaginal despite history
Corneal involvement → urgent ophthalmology; avoid unsupervised ocular corticosteroids

rows.label: Complications
items: Encephalitis, aseptic meningitis, urinary retention, keratitis, dissemination; increased HIV acquisition risk
Acyclovir → crystal nephropathy, neurotoxicity with renal impairment; hydrate, adjust dose

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Avoid sex during lesions/prodrome**, condoms, partner disclosure; suppression lowers but never eliminates transmission
Avoid kissing infants with active labialis; cover lesions, hand hygiene

rows.label: Mimics
items: Syphilis: classically painless chancre; chancroid: deep purulent painful ulcer
Aphthae: mucosal ulcers, no preceding vesicles
Zoster: unilateral dermatomal eruption
Felon/paronychia: pus, no vesicles; whitlow → oral acyclovir, **no incision/drainage**

herpes-simplex-virus.evidence: Checked genital disease 2026-10-30: [CDC HSV guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/std/treatment-guidelines/herpes.htm); neonatal/eczema management established teaching.

table.title: Neonatal IV acyclovir duration
rows: ≥21 days; CNS: confirm CSF PCR clearance

hyperemesis-gravidarum.name: Hyperemesis gravidarum
hyperemesis-gravidarum.scope: Nausea and vomiting of pregnancy, ketonuria, electrolyte abnormalities, Wernicke encephalopathy, dietary modifications, antiemetics, IV hydration
hyperemesis-gravidarum.core: Severe early-pregnancy nausea and vomiting with inability to eat/drink normally, impaired functioning, and often dehydration or weight loss.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Previous hyperemesis, multiple gestation, molar pregnancy, family history; begins usually before 16 weeks

rows.label: Clues
items: Orthostasis, tachycardia, reduced urine, weight loss often >5% prepregnancy weight
Hypokalemia, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis; starvation may produce ketosis/acidosis
★ Confusion, ataxia, ophthalmoplegia → **Wernicke encephalopathy**; triad may be incomplete
Mild transaminitis or transient low TSH can occur; fever/focal abdominal pain suggests another diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental hormonal signals, including GDF15, drive nausea; prolonged starvation depletes thiamine and electrolytes
Gestational transient thyrotoxicosis reflects hCG stimulation rather than intrinsic thyroid autoimmunity

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical assessment of intake, weight and hydration; electrolytes, renal function, urinalysis, liver tests
Ultrasound assesses gestational dating, multiplicity, or suspected trophoblastic disease
★ **Ketonuria not required, not a severity marker**; older exam questions may expect urine ketones for starvation/dehydration
Thyroid testing for severe/atypical cases; goiter or ophthalmopathy suggests Graves rather than pregnancy physiology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Mild nausea: small frequent meals, avoid triggers; **pyridoxine + doxylamine** first-line
Persistent vomiting → promethazine, metoclopramide, or ondansetron; combine agents from different classes if needed
★ Dehydration/electrolytes, PO intolerance → **admit: IV saline + potassium**, parenteral antiemetics; replace low magnesium
Prolonged vomiting → thiamine before dextrose; suspected Wernicke → high-dose IV thiamine immediately
Refractory disease → enteral nutrition preferred; corticosteroids after other options fail

rows.label: Complications
items: AKI, malnutrition, esophageal injury, venous thrombosis; severe electrolyte abnormalities → arrhythmia
Refeeding syndrome during nutritional recovery; monitor phosphorus, magnesium, potassium
Nonsevere disease, mild weight loss → no significant fetal harm; severe disease → low birth weight

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early antiemetics in recurrent disease; maintain hydration/nutrition; hospitalized patients need VTE-risk assessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Gastroenteritis: diarrhea, infectious contacts, short nonpregnancy-linked course
DKA: hyperglycemia or euglycemic pregnancy ketoacidosis with high anion gap
Appendicitis: focal progressive tenderness and inflammatory signs

hyperemesis-gravidarum.evidence: Ketones/thiamine checked 2026-10-30: [RCOG Green-top 69, 2024](https://doi.org/10.1111/1471-0528.17739); remaining content established teaching.

infertility.name: Infertility
infertility.scope: Definition (failure to conceive after 12 months), initial evaluation, semen analysis (male factor), ovulatory status (midluteal progesterone), tubal and uterine factors (hysterosalpingography), ovarian reserve testing
infertility.core: No conception after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse; evaluate after 6 months at age ≥35, immediately over 40 or with risks.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, PCOS, endometriosis, PID, pelvic surgery, chemotherapy, testicular injury, exogenous testosterone
Smoking, marked weight extremes, premature ovarian insufficiency, untreated endocrine disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Irregular/absent cycles → ovulatory dysfunction; galactorrhea → hyperprolactinemia; hot flashes → ovarian insufficiency
Prior ectopic pregnancy or chlamydia → tubal damage; normal cycles do not exclude male factor

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Failure of sperm production/delivery, oocyte release, fertilization, transport, or implantation; mixed factors common
Estrogen → proliferative endometrium; LH surge → ovulation
Corpus luteum **progesterone** → secretory endometrium, ↑basal body temperature

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Evaluate **both partners simultaneously**; reproductive history, sexual timing, examinations; semen analysis early
Abnormal semen result → repeat and male reproductive evaluation; do not begin with female laparoscopy
★ Ovulation uncertain → **progesterone about 7 days before expected menses**; >3 ng/mL supports ovulation
Regular 21–35-day cycles usually imply ovulation; targeted TSH, prolactin only for relevant symptoms
★ Ovulatory + normal semen → **HSG** (tubes) before laparoscopy; saline sonography: cavity; avoid in pregnancy/infection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Anovulation/PCOS → **letrozole**, clomiphene alternative; hyperprolactinemia → cabergoline; correct thyroid disease
Tubal occlusion/severe male factor → IVF, sometimes intracytoplasmic sperm injection
Unexplained infertility → ovarian stimulation with intrauterine insemination, then IVF if unsuccessful
Intercourse every 1–2 days during fertile window; avoid testosterone for fertility-seeking men

rows.label: Complications
items: Psychological distress; stimulation → ovarian hyperstimulation, multiple gestation; assisted reproduction → ectopic pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: STI prevention, tobacco cessation, weight optimization; fertility preservation before gonadotoxic treatment
Preconception folic acid and medication review

rows.label: Mimics
items: Infrequent intercourse: inadequate exposure despite normal reproductive testing
Recurrent pregnancy loss: conception occurs, followed by repeated losses

table.title: Ovarian reserve: treatment response, not natural fertility
rows: Low values suggest reduced follicular pool

infertility.evidence: Evaluation checked 2026-10-30: [ASRM 2021](https://www.asrm.org/practice-guidance/practice-committee-documents/fertility-evaluation-of-infertile-women-a-committee-opinion-2021/); treatment established reproductive guidance.

intra-amniotic-infection.name: Intra-amniotic infection
intra-amniotic-infection.scope: Chorioamnionitis, clinical diagnostic criteria (maternal fever, fetal tachycardia, purulent fluid, uterine tenderness), IV ampicillin and gentamicin, labor augmentation, postpartum endometritis
intra-amniotic-infection.core: Intrapartum fever with fetal tachycardia or purulent cervical drainage suggests ascending infection requiring antibiotics and delivery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prolonged membrane rupture, prolonged labor, repeated digital examinations after rupture, internal monitoring
Genital tract colonization; infection can occur with intact membranes

rows.label: Clues
items: Uterine tenderness, foul amniotic fluid, maternal tachycardia, leukocytosis
Hypotension, altered mentation, oliguria → maternal sepsis; leukocytosis alone nonspecific during labor

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Polymicrobial ascent from vagina into decidua, membranes, amniotic fluid, and fetus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected infection: temperature **≥39°C**, or **38–38.9°C plus one additional clinical risk factor**
Additional factors: fetal baseline >160/min, purulent cervical drainage, maternal leukocytosis without corticosteroids
ACOG 2024 permits diagnosis without fever when other clinical findings strongly support infection
Clinical diagnosis; placental histology or amniotic-fluid testing confirms retrospectively; never delay treatment
Sepsis → blood cultures, lactate, CBC, renal function; cultures before antibiotics only without delay

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Prompt **IV ampicillin + gentamicin**, acetaminophen, IV fluids; notify neonatal team
★ Induce/augment labor with **oxytocin**; infection alone is not a cesarean indication
Cesarean for obstetric indication → add clindamycin for anaerobic coverage; postpartum dosing depends on course
Shock → fluid resuscitation, norepinephrine, urgent source control; do not await fetal lung maturity

rows.label: Complications
items: Uterine atony/hemorrhage, postpartum endometritis, bacteremia, septic shock
Neonatal pneumonia, sepsis, meningitis; prematurity-related morbidity
Endometritis: mixed aerobes/anaerobes; risks **cesarean** (strongest), prolonged rupture; shock → puerperal sepsis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Minimize digital examinations after rupture; timely term-PROM induction; PPROM latency antibiotics when expectant

rows.label: Mimics
items: Epidural-associated fever: sterile inflammation possible; cannot dismiss coexisting infection
★ Postpartum endometritis: fever, fundal tenderness → IV **clindamycin + gentamicin** first; older exams: ampicillin + gentamicin
Pyelonephritis: flank tenderness and positive urine culture

intra-amniotic-infection.evidence: Diagnostic update checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG 2024](https://doi.org/10.1097/aog.0000000000005593); management follows established ACOG teaching.

intrahepatic-cholestasis-of-pregnancy.name: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy
intrahepatic-cholestasis-of-pregnancy.scope: Pruritus of palms and soles without rash, elevated total bile acids and transaminases, ursodeoxycholic acid, fetal risks (intrauterine fetal demise, meconium passage), delivery timing at 36-37 weeks
intrahepatic-cholestasis-of-pregnancy.core: Late-pregnancy palm/sole pruritus without a primary rash suggests cholestasis; biochemical severity guides fetal-risk counseling and planned birth.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Previous cholestasis, family history, multiple gestation, estrogen exposure; chronic hepatobiliary disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Nocturnal generalized itching, excoriations from scratching; occasional jaundice/dark urine
Usually third trimester; marked abdominal pain, fever, hypertension or confusion suggests another disorder

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pregnancy hormones impair susceptible hepatocyte bile transport → maternal/fetal bile-acid accumulation
Fetal arrhythmia/placental vascular effects may cause sudden events despite reassuring surveillance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Total serum bile acids + AST/ALT**; bilirubin usually normal or mildly elevated
Bile acids above laboratory pregnancy threshold support diagnosis; >10 µmol/L traditionally used in US teaching
Persistent symptoms with normal initial results → repeat testing; itching can precede biochemical elevation
Rule out viral hepatitis/drug injury; RUQ ultrasound for obstructive signs; check platelets/BP for HELLP
Alkaline phosphatase physiologically rises in pregnancy and does not establish diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Ursodeoxycholic acid** first-line for maternal itching; counsel that fetal protection is unproven
★ **Bile acids ≥100 µmol/L → delivery at 36 weeks**
★ Below 100 → deliver **36–39 weeks**, earlier within window for ≥40 or additional risks
Antenatal testing when an abnormal result would prompt birth; normal NST does not eliminate stillbirth risk
Birth before 37 weeks → corticosteroids if not previously received; biochemical confirmation required for preterm delivery

rows.label: Complications
items: Stillbirth, meconium-stained fluid, spontaneous/iatrogenic preterm birth, neonatal respiratory morbidity
Rare vitamin K deficiency with prolonged cholestasis → bleeding; postpartum persistence suggests underlying liver disease

rows.label: Prevention
items: High recurrence risk: counsel and assess symptoms early in subsequent pregnancy
Repeat bile acids/liver tests postpartum to document resolution; reconsider estrogen contraception if symptoms recur

rows.label: Mimics
items: Polymorphic eruption of pregnancy: visible urticarial plaques beginning in abdominal striae
Pemphigoid gestationis: periumbilical eruption progressing to blisters
HELLP/acute fatty liver: systemic illness, thrombocytopenia or hypoglycemia, not isolated itching

intrahepatic-cholestasis-of-pregnancy.evidence: Timing checked 2026-10-30: [SMFM Consult 53](https://publications.smfm.org/publications/374-society-for-maternal-fetal-medicine-consult-series-53/); scope's blanket 36–37-week timing requires bile-acid stratification.

intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.name: Intrapartum fetal monitoring
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.scope: Baseline fetal heart rate, variability, early decelerations, late decelerations, variable decelerations, category I II III tracings, intrauterine resuscitation
intrapartum-fetal-monitoring.core: Fetal oxygenation assessment from baseline, variability, and decelerations; persistent category III requires expedited delivery after immediate resuscitation.

rows.label: Definition
items: ★ Normal baseline **110–160/min**; moderate variability **6–25 beats/min**
Bradycardia <110; tachycardia >160; baseline change lasts ≥10 minutes
Tachysystole: >5 contractions/10 minutes over 30 minutes; oxytocin excess → late decelerations

rows.label: Interpret
items: Early: mirrors contraction → head compression; benign
Late: nadir after contraction peak → uteroplacental insufficiency
Variable: abrupt fall → cord compression; prolonged: 2–10 minutes

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Category II: lateral positioning, stop oxytocin, IV fluids; correct hypotension
Persistent tachysystole with concerning tracing → **terbutaline**; recurrent variables → amnioinfusion
★ Bradycardia: exam for cord prolapse; post-epidural → **maternal hypotension**; prepare delivery

rows.label: Compare
items: **Maternal fever** commonest tachycardia, variability kept; hypoxia → low variability, late decelerations
Transient minimal variability, no decelerations → **fetal sleep**, usually <40 minutes
Late decelerations → hypoxemia → **metabolic acidosis**; acute cord compression → respiratory acidosis

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Oxygen only for **maternal hypoxemia**; older routine-oxygen answers conflict with current guidance
Moderate variability or accelerations strongly argues against current metabolic acidemia
Category II alone does not mandate cesarean; reassess response and labor progress

table.title: Three-tier interpretation
rows: Reassuring rate/variability; no late or variable decelerations
Absent variability + recurrent late/variable decelerations or bradycardia
Resuscitate; unresolved → cesarean unless fully dilated
Evaluate severe anemia; expedite if persistent

macrocytic-anemia.name: Macrocytic anemia
macrocytic-anemia.scope: Folate deficiency, vitamin B12 deficiency, pernicious anemia, hypersegmented neutrophils, methylmalonic acid and homocysteine
macrocytic-anemia.core: MCV >100 fL prompts separation of megaloblastic DNA-synthesis failure from alcohol, liver disease, hypothyroidism, reticulocytosis, and marrow disorders.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Vegan diet without supplementation, gastric bypass, ileal disease/resection, metformin, long-term **PPI** → B12 depletion
Alcohol misuse, poor intake, pregnancy, methotrexate, trimethoprim → folate depletion; stores last months, B12 years
Autoimmune gastritis → pernicious anemia; nitrous oxide functionally inactivates cobalamin

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, glossitis; ineffective erythropoiesis may raise LDH/indirect bilirubin and lower other cell lines
★ **Paresthesias, gait ataxia, impaired vibration/proprioception** → B12 deficiency, even without anemia
Smooth macro-ovalocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils indicate megaloblastic change

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Defective thymidine synthesis delays nuclear maturation relative to cytoplasm
B12-dependent myelin metabolism explains spinal cord/peripheral nerve injury; folate deficiency lacks this syndrome
B12 malabsorption corrected by oral intrinsic factor → **gastric IF loss** (atrophic gastritis), not ileal disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC, smear, reticulocytes, B12**; assess folate, liver tests, TSH, exposures
Borderline B12 → methylmalonic acid; renal impairment can elevate it independently
★ Suspected pernicious anemia → **anti-intrinsic-factor antibodies**; highly specific but not fully sensitive
High reticulocytes → bleeding/hemolysis; unexplained cytopenias/dysplasia → bone marrow evaluation for MDS
Coexisting iron deficiency may normalize MCV; neurologic suspicion still requires B12 evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Replace B12 before or with folate**; folate alone can conceal ongoing neurologic injury
Neurologic/severe deficiency or malabsorption → parenteral B12 initially; irreversible cause requires lifelong replacement
Dietary B12 deficiency may respond to high-dose oral replacement; folate deficiency → oral folic acid
Remove causative drug/exposure where possible; monitor reticulocyte response and count recovery

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated B12 deficiency → irreversible neurologic disability; severe disease → pancytopenia
Pernicious anemia → increased gastric adenocarcinoma and neuroendocrine tumor risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Reliable B12 supplementation for vegans**; lifelong monitoring/replacement after relevant GI surgery
Folic acid before conception and early pregnancy; improve nutrition and reduce harmful alcohol intake

rows.label: Mimics
items: Alcohol-associated macrocytosis: round macrocytes, no required megaloblastic change
Myelodysplasia: persistent multilineage cytopenia, dysplastic marrow
Reticulocytosis: polychromasia after blood loss or hemolysis

macrocytic-anemia.evidence: Not checked online; established hematology and nutritional teaching.

menopause.name: Menopause
menopause.scope: Perimenopause, menopause transition, vasomotor symptoms, genitourinary syndrome of menopause, HRT
menopause.core: Menopause is 12 months without menses from ovarian follicle depletion; manage bothersome symptoms according to uterine status and hormone-treatment risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Natural transition typically in late 40s–50s; smoking, oophorectomy, chemotherapy or pelvic radiation accelerate onset
Menopause before 40 suggests primary ovarian insufficiency and requires a separate evaluation

rows.label: Clues
items: Perimenopause: variable cycles, skipped periods, fertility remains; isolated irregularity → **reassurance**, no biopsy
Vasomotor episodes: abrupt heat, flushing, sweating, disturbed sleep; mood symptoms can coexist
Genitourinary syndrome: dryness, dyspareunia, urinary urgency and recurrent UTIs; pale thin friable mucosa
Urogenital estrogen loss: **negative cultures**, possible sterile pyuria; friable mucosa → spotting, postcoital bleeding

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ↓Follicles → ↓estradiol/inhibin and ↑FSH; hypothalamic thermoregulatory changes drive hot flashes
Urogenital estrogen deficiency thins epithelium, raises vaginal pH and changes flora

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical symptoms at **≥45 years → clinical diagnosis**; routine FSH unnecessary
Unexpected amenorrhea → pregnancy test; earlier menopause → FSH/estradiol and targeted thyroid/prolactin evaluation
Postmenopausal bleeding → endometrial evaluation; do not attribute to normal transition
Hormonal contraception alters bleeding/FSH interpretation; amenorrhea on contraception alone does not establish menopause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Bothersome hot flashes, low risk, generally <60 or within 10 years → **systemic estrogen**
★ Intact uterus → **add progestogen**; hysterectomy → estrogen alone usually sufficient
Avoid systemic hormones with unexplained bleeding, estrogen-sensitive cancer, prior VTE/stroke/MI or active liver disease
Hormones unsuitable → **venlafaxine, paroxetine or gabapentin**; selected fezolinetant requires liver monitoring
★ Isolated GSM → lubricants/moisturizers then **low-dose vaginal estrogen**; routine progestogen generally unnecessary

rows.label: Complications
items: Bone loss, fracture, sexual dysfunction; oral systemic estrogen increases VTE/stroke risk
Combined systemic hormones can increase breast cancer risk; unopposed uterine estrogen causes endometrial hyperplasia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Weight-bearing exercise, adequate calcium/vitamin D, smoking cessation; age/risk-based osteoporosis screening
Hormone treatment not for primary cardiovascular/dementia prevention; reassess symptoms and risks periodically
Continue contraception during transition until menopause criteria met; menopausal hormones do not prevent pregnancy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperthyroidism: persistent heat intolerance, tachycardia, suppressed TSH
Pregnancy: positive hCG despite irregular cycles

multiple-gestation.name: Multiple gestation
multiple-gestation.scope: Dichorionic diamniotic (lambda sign), monochorionic diamniotic (T-sign), monochorionic monoamniotic, twin-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS), selective FGR, delivery timing recommendations
multiple-gestation.core: Chorionicity and amnionicity determine twin-specific surveillance, complications, and delivery timing; establish both on first-trimester ultrasound.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dizygotic twins: ovulation induction/assisted reproduction, maternal age, family history
Monozygotic splitting timing determines placental and sac sharing

rows.label: Clues
items: Uterus larger than dates, exaggerated pregnancy symptoms; ultrasound confirms fetal number
★ Shared placenta with **oligohydramnios/polyhydramnios sequence** → TTTS; small/absent donor bladder
Selective FGR: one small twin, discordant estimated weights; assess each umbilical artery Doppler

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental vascular anastomoses permit imbalanced flow in monochorionic twins
Donor hypovolemia reduces urine; recipient hypervolemia increases urine and cardiac strain

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **First-trimester ultrasound** identifies shared placenta and intertwin membrane
Monochorionic diamniotic → ultrasound **every 2 weeks from 16 weeks** for fluid/bladders
Serial growth in all twins; Doppler and more frequent assessment when growth discordance develops
TTTS donor deepest pocket ≤2 cm, recipient ≥8 cm; staging incorporates bladder, Doppler, hydrops

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ TTTS stages II–IV at 16–26 weeks → **fetoscopic laser ablation** of placental anastomoses
Asymptomatic stage I → at least weekly surveillance; refer fetal intervention center if progression/symptoms
★ Diamniotic twins with **first twin cephalic** may deliver vaginally with experienced team
Monoamniotic twins → cesarean; fetal deterioration, preeclampsia, or severe growth issues may require earlier delivery

rows.label: Complications
items: Preterm birth, preeclampsia, anemia, gestational diabetes, postpartum hemorrhage
Monoamniotic cord entanglement; monochorionic co-twin death can cause surviving twin neurologic injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Low-dose aspirin for preeclampsia prevention; optimize iron/nutrition; single-embryo transfer reduces iatrogenic multiples

rows.label: Mimics
items: Incorrect dates/macrosomia: enlarged uterus but singleton on imaging
Twin anemia-polycythemia sequence: discordant MCA velocities without major fluid imbalance

neural-tube-defects.name: Neural tube defects
neural-tube-defects.scope: Anencephaly, spina bifida occulta, meningocele, myelomeningocele, Chiari II malformation, maternal serum AFP, amniotic acetylcholinesterase, lemon and banana signs, folic acid prevention
neural-tube-defects.core: Neural tube closure failure by approximately 4 weeks after conception produces cranial or spinal defects; prevention must begin before pregnancy recognition.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Low folate, prior affected pregnancy, maternal diabetes/obesity, valproate/carbamazepine, early-pregnancy hyperthermia

rows.label: Clues
items: Midline lumbosacral sac, lower-limb weakness, absent reflexes, bladder dysfunction with neural involvement
★ **Lemon skull and banana cerebellum** on fetal ultrasound suggest open spina bifida/Chiari II
Occult lesions: hair tuft, atypical deep dimple, hemangioma; normal skin does not guarantee normal cord

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Failed neurulation leaves neural tissue unprotected; CSF leakage contributes to hindbrain herniation
Folate supports nucleotide synthesis during rapid embryonic cell division

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Maternal serum **AFP at 15–22 weeks**; elevation → verify dating/number, detailed ultrasound
Open defects elevate AFP; closed occulta may not; cfDNA does not screen neural tube defects
★ Uncertain imaging → amniotic fluid **AFP and acetylcholinesterase**; target anatomy scan at 18–22 weeks
Postnatal spinal ultrasound in young infant or MRI for suspected occult dysraphism/tethered cord

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Open spinal lesion: **prone positioning, sterile saline dressing**, avoid pressure/contamination; neonatal neurosurgery
Early closure; assess hydrocephalus, renal function and bladder emptying; intermittent catheterization when neurogenic
Selected prenatal myelomeningocele repair can improve motor outcomes/reduce shunting, with maternal and prematurity risks
Anencephaly → counseling, pregnancy options, and palliative neonatal care; no curative treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Hydrocephalus (Chiari II obstructs CSF), meningitis, orthopedic deformities, neurogenic bowel/bladder, recurrent UTI, kidney injury
Tethered cord may cause progressive weakness or continence changes during growth
Osteopenic insensate legs: new swelling → **X-ray** for occult fracture

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Folic acid 400–800 µg/day** before conception through early pregnancy for average risk
Prior NTD pregnancy → **4 mg/day**, starting ≥1 month before conception through first 3 months
Optimize diabetes, review antiseizure drugs before pregnancy; avoid prolonged overheating

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sacrococcygeal teratoma: solid/cystic mass, not exposed neural placode
Abdominal wall defect: elevated AFP but bowel outside abdomen on ultrasound

table.title: Lesions
rows: Meninges/CSF herniate; cord remains within canal

neural-tube-defects.evidence: Folate checked 2026-10-30: [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/folic-acid/hcp/clinical-overview/), [USPSTF 2023](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/document/ClinicalSummaryFinal/folic-acid-for-the-prevention-of-neural-tube-defects-preventive-medication); remaining content established teaching.

normal-and-abnormal-labor.name: Normal and abnormal labor
